order.why_here: The baseline scan: one read index, one start marker, and always emitting the final piece.
Introduces the counter: forget order, keep a 26-cell histogram, the first canonical form.
Two pointers on a mutable copy: read/write compaction, then reverse-all and reverse-each.
Two strings scanned in lockstep with integers parsed in place; an exhausted pointer reads as zero.
The first explicit state machine (SPACE, SIGN, DIGITS, STOP) with overflow clamped during accumulation.
The state machine becomes a grammar: three flags, and exact rules for which transition resets which flag.
The stack arrives: '..' cancels the most recent surviving directory name.
A stack of indices, so unmatched characters can be marked and dropped in one pass.
Back to a plain scan with a row pointer that bounces between walls; the 2-D picture is unnecessary.
Canonical keys generalised from sorted letters to gaps between letters mod 26.
Formatting instead of parsing: chunk by thousands and apply one rule per chunk with lookup tables.
Hard cut-and-reassemble: greedy line packing, then divmod to spread spaces with the remainder on the left.
First self-comparison: grow mirrors outward from 2n - 1 centres.
Borders and the KMP failure function, built incrementally with fallback to the border of the border.
Reuses the failure function on s + '#' + reverse(s) to find the longest palindromic prefix.
Combines palindrome checks with canonical lookup: reversed words in a hash map, every cut of every word.
Rolling hash plus binary search on the answer length; windows compared in O(1) each.
